title: Crosses of many lands

lines: A SMALL CROSS ON THE WRIST.
A RING, A LACE, A SLANTED BAR.
cards: On the inside of a wrist, just below the palm, a small blue cross, inked into the skin. It doesn't wash off. Some Coptic Christians in Egypt wear one for life.

Lay other crosses beside it. A gray stone cross in an Irish field, taller than a man, with a ring around its center. A silver cross from Ethiopia, held in a priest's hand, its arms opening into patterns like lace.
A cross from a Russian church with three bars, the lowest one slanting. Four lands, four shapes, all pointing to the same cross.

teach.h: CELTIC: A RING AROUND THE CENTER.
teach.b: Start in Ireland and Scotland, with the Celtic cross: a ring around the place where the arms meet. What did the ring first mean?
Some see a halo, some the sun, some a circle with no end; others think it helped hold the stone arms up. The stone doesn't explain itself. Next, Egypt.

teach.h: COPTIC: A CROSS ON THE WRIST.
teach.b: Some Coptic Christians carry a small cross tattooed on the inner wrist, some from childhood: a way of belonging that can't be taken off. Paul wrote to the Galatians, "I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus."
Many readers take him to mean his scars. A wrist cross is a gentler mark, worn in the same spirit. Then Ethiopia.

teach.h: ETHIOPIAN: A HAND CROSS LIKE LACE.
teach.b: Priests there may carry a hand cross of metal or wood, its arms opening into woven patterns, and people come up to kiss it and be blessed. Styles differ from place to place and maker to maker.
Last, the Russian Orthodox cross. The top bar stands for Pilate's sign. John says: "And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS."
When the chief priests asked him to change it, Pilate said: "What I have written I have written."
The slanted bottom bar is a footrest, and Orthodox tradition says it tilts up toward the thief who asked to be remembered.
Under them all, one line from Luke: "If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me."

how: Christians in different lands carry the cross in their own forms: Celtic high crosses with a ring, small crosses tattooed on the wrist by some Coptic Christians, Ethiopian hand crosses carried by priests to bless people, and three-barred crosses in Russian and other Orthodox churches.

games.q: what does “crosses of many lands” mean?
o: the cross, shaped differently by each land that carries it
the crosses set up along roads to mark old borders
crosses brought home by pilgrims from the Holy Land

games.q: crosses of many lands — tap the pairs.
p: a small cross on the inner wrist

s: every cross has exactly two bars
the Russian Orthodox cross has three: Pilate's sign at the top and a slanted footrest below.
everyone agrees what the Celtic ring first meant
the stone doesn't say. some see a halo, some the sun, some a circle with no end.
the Orthodox cross's top bar recalls Pilate's sign
"JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS," the title John says Pilate put on the cross.

games.q: you're Pilate. you've had a sign put on the cross. the chief priests ask you to change its words. what do you say?
o: fine, change it however you like.
"what I have written I have written."
games.why: Pilate refuses: "what I have written I have written." the Orthodox cross still carries that sign as its top bar.

practice: With pen and paper, draw one cross from another land, the Celtic ring, the Orthodox slanted foot, or an Ethiopian cross's patterned arms, and give its one special detail your care.

As you draw, think of the people who carry that shape: in a field, on a wrist, in a priest's hand. If you pray, you can pray for them as you draw; if you don't, let the drawing be a way of paying attention to strangers.

wordCard.voice: Crosses of many lands. Ringed, inked, woven, three-barred: one cross, shaped by the places that carry it.

orig.note: Ge'ez and Amharic: cross. Ethiopian Christians keep a feast of the Cross by this name.

carryVoice: Your line: many crosses. Each land shaped the same sign its own way. Until tomorrow.
